reason: Verification failed due to missing run loop, incomplete results(), and absent disease dynamics. With 3 iterations left, there is clear potential to reach spec-compliance by implementing a minimal SEIR model, wiring run/main, and completing required metrics. The current codebase has a solid scaffold (agents, network, market, policy), so targeted fixes can yield substantial improvements quickly.

specific_areas: Implement Simulation.run() and wire main() to instantiate Simulation, execute the T-day loop, and print results JSON.

Complete Simulation.results() to return all required metrics: adoption_rate_over_time, peak_adoption with day, time_to_reach_70_percent, average_compliance, infections_over_time (daily and cumulative), infections_averted, effective_reproduction_number_Re, disparity_in_adoption_by_income, policy_cost, mask_supply_utilization.

Add a minimal SEIR process in step(): S/E/I/R states, initialization via initial_infection_prevalence, per-day progression, transmission per contact modified by mask effectiveness (source and wearer) and ventilation; track infections_ts and Re.
Model mandate enforcement and fines: compute compliance rate, apply enforcement checks, levy fine_amount on non-compliant agents to budgets, accumulate policy_cost, and record compliance_ts.
Compute infections_averted by running an internal no-mask counterfactual (same seed and disease params, zero mask effectiveness/mandate) and subtract cumulative infections.
Market and utilization: scale target_inventory to ~20% of population; track masks_sold_cum and masks_distributed_cum; compute mask_supply_utilization = sold / total available.
Remove the adoption clamp on mandate activation and stray pass statements; remove redundant clamp around sigmoid; ensure time_to_reach_70_percent is computed.
Introduce minimal budget replenishment (e.g., weekly) to avoid permanent lockout and hook adherence_decay_rate and wealth_effect_on_adoption where straightforward.
